firstScreen.notes: qa/screens/1440x900-first.png: h1 'Small fixes for old Louisville houses' readable at 0ms, phone in header, Price a visit CTA above fold, street-sign marker visible at left establishing signature. Trade + city + action clear within 5 seconds.

distinctiveness.notes: qa/screens/1440x900-full.png: street-sign marker system organizing by neighborhood is distinctive for handyman niche; no sibling uses this. Bourbon Barrel palette reads Louisville-specific. However dotted walking path between stops is absent from build, weakening the walk thesis. Sign markers read as subtle labels rather than architectural elements.

type.notes: qa/screens/390x844-first.png: Aleo slab serif carries old-sign character on headlines and sign blades. Figtree legible at all sizes. DM Mono adds utilitarian texture to house types and prices. H1 clamp works across viewports. Kicker line shares mono styling with price labels creating slight hierarchy confusion.

layout.notes: qa/screens/1440x900-full.png: eleven sections follow blueprint, tone sequence passes rhythm rules. Sign-rail layout repeats four times creating visual monotony — Highlands and Crescent Hill feel identical structurally. Full-bleed break band provides breath. Pricing table and checklist stack break pattern appropriately.

photo.notes: qa/screens/1440x900-full.png: all photos are placeholders with descriptive fallback panels. Captions describe frames accurately without inventing jobs. No faces, logos or house numbers. Photo grade filter applied consistently. Cannot score higher until real media curated.

copy.notes: qa/screens/390x844-full.png: voice matches brief — specific to Louisville house types, honest about limits, no banned words. Service blurbs use homeowner language. Sample labels present on all reviews and pricing. Meta description within length limit. Honest-limits callout could be tighter.

mobile.notes: qa/screens/390x844-first.png: mobile bar present with call + CTA meeting 48px tap targets. Header collapses to hamburger correctly. Sign markers readable at narrow widths. Form inputs meet touch target size. Offset-frame hero stacks cleanly. No horizontal scroll.

a11y.notes: dist/index.html: skip link present, semantic landmarks used, ARIA labels on navs. Focus styles 3px outline. Reduced motion disables animations, shows content statically. Form has fieldset/legend. Star ratings have aria-labels. Color contrast meets WCAG AA.

motion.notes: qa/screens/1440x900-full.png: hero swing via CSS keyframes gated by sw-motion. Sign flip-up via ScrollTrigger works. Reveal and clip-reveal patterns functional. Dotted walking path connecting neighborhood stops is absent — key signature motion story missing. Without it the walk thesis feels incomplete.

wow.notes: qa/screens/1440x900-mid.png: Derby-ready porch checklist functions correctly with hour-band estimate and form pre-fill. Seasonal relevance smart. Visually reads as standard form rather than distinctive tool. T-accent band helps but checklist items lack tactile design.

polish.notes: qa/screens/1440x900-full.png: no orphan words in headlines. Button hover underlines animate smoothly. Sample tags styled consistently. Progress bar tracks scroll. Overall finish clean but not exceptional — missing walking path and uniform sign-rail layouts prevent higher score.

elevate.move: Implement the dotted walking path SVG that draws down the page between neighborhood stops, driven by --sw-p, so the signature motion story is complete and the neighborhood walk thesis is visually realized.

Break sign-rail monotony by giving Highlands a split-text layout with honest-limits callout integrated into composition, and Crescent Hill a card-grid layout for its four services instead of repeating the list format.
